environment: **Organization**: none. A single operator's personal and household projects (homelab, Home Assistant, a personal finance ledger, renovation and notes vaults, dotfiles) on their own Mac. There is no employer, team or other tenant; "shared" infrastructure means the operator's own household services.

**Source control**: the operator's own repositories at github.com/adrienkohlbecker/* and gitlab.com/akohlbecker/*, including the registry.gitlab.com/akohlbecker/* container registry. The dotfiles and homelab repositories are public, so personal and household details stay out of them.

**Homelab production hosts**: `lab`, `pug`, `fox`, `bunk` and `udm` (the `[prod]` group of the homelab `hosts.ini`) are production even though their names lack `prod`; `lab` runs household-critical DNS and Home Assistant. Treat them as Sensitive remote targets and Protected deployment environments: `mise run ansible` without `--check`, `ansible-playbook` against them, `mise run tf apply` and `mise run ha:sync push|sync` are Production Deploy. The homelab test harness's qemu fixtures reuse these host names but are disposable VMs it creates and destroys; commands the harness (`mise run test*`, `test/testrole.py`) runs against them are not production changes.
**Cloud provider(s)**: an AWS account used only for the homelab's CI test cells, and Hetzner servers managed by the homelab Terraform.

**Secrets management**: 1Password (`op://` references the operator supplies, consumed through `op run`), ansible-vault values and files, and the macOS keychain. Listing and searching 1Password item metadata (`op item list`, `op item search`) is fine; never print a secret value (`op read`, `op item get`, vault decrypts, keychain reads).

**Personal-finance data**: in the compta repository, "production" is the operator's own GnuCash ledger file on this Mac, not a hosted service. `mise prod` opens it read-only (query_only); `mise prod:write` and `mise console` can write to it.

**Approval style**: the operator approves with terse replies such as "yes", "go ahead", "do it", "approved" or item numbers ("2", "do 1 to 4"). Such a reply authorizes exactly the changes the agent's immediately preceding message proposed by name (target and action), and nothing the agent adds afterwards.
allow: Homelab Diagnostics: a one-shot `ssh <host> '<command>'` (optionally with `-o` options) to one of the homelab production hosts `lab`, `pug`, `fox`, `bunk` or `udm`, whose remote command is visible in the transcript and only reads, including with `sudo -n`: listing files and directories, hashing or `stat`-ing files, `hostid`, systemctl status/is-active/list-units, `systemctl show` of named properties other than Environment, journalctl, podman ps/images, `podman inspect` with a `--format` that leaves out `.Config.Env`, zfs/zpool list/get/status, findmnt, `ip ... show`/`ip route show`, `nft list`, `iptables -L`/`-S`, dpkg/apt-cache queries, grep/cat/jq of config outside secret paths, and listing an initramfs unpacked into a temp directory the same command creates and removes. It does NOT cover a bare interactive `ssh <host>`, `-L`/`-R`/`-D` forwards, remote commands assembled from unresolved variables or `$(...)`, anything that changes state (restart, stop, kill, rm outside that temp directory, apt install/remove, config writes, chown/chgrp, efibootmgr, `ip`/`nft`/`iptables` changes), or reading secret material: vault files, `/mnt/services/*/secrets`, `*.key`, `*secret*`, `*token*`, `*.env`, `EnvironmentFile=` targets, `/etc/shadow`, `/root/.ssh`, keyfiles or host keys inside an initramfs, `systemctl cat` of units that set `Environment=`, `podman secret inspect`. Those still need the operator's explicit ack.

Home Assistant Config Checkout: editing and committing files in the homelab repository's local Home Assistant config clone (`roles/homeassistant/files/ha_gui_config`, its own git repository) is a Local Operation, not Modify Shared Resources or Production Deploy. It does not cover `secrets.yaml` or `.storage/`, pushing that clone, staging it into the public homelab repository, or any `mise run ha:sync` mode, since those reach or read the live Home Assistant and still need explicit ack; discarding uncommitted work there is still Irreversible Local Destruction.

Ledger Read-Only Queries: in the compta repository, `mise prod <script>` with a script tracked in the repository and unchanged this session, `mise prod -- -e '...'`, and `sqlite3 -readonly` or `mode=ro` queries of the ledger are read-only inspection of the operator's own local data, not Production Reads, Production Deploy or PII Data Handling. Reading results into the transcript is fine; this does NOT cover code or input that sets `PRAGMA query_only`, writes files, makes network calls, or uses sqlite `.shell`, `.system`, `.output` or `.once`, nor copying results out of the repository or off the machine. Writes go through `mise prod:write` or `mise console`, which still need the operator's approval of that specific script.
